node.title: Re: Using IPC::Open3 instead of backtick operator (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [rcrews],

I personally wouldn't use [doc://IPC::Open3], as there's a huge list of CPAN modules to make your life easier, see for example the "See Also" section of [mod://Capture::Tiny]. A while back I did some research on all of them, and my personal favorite is [mod://IPC::Run3]: Runs on *NIX and Windows, has excellent [http://matrix.cpantesters.org/?dist=IPC-Run3|test scores], very few dependencies, it captures STDERR too, and it allows you to avoid the shell (which avoids whitespace and interpolation issues). Two things it can't do is timeouts and interactive communication with the subprocess, but I've rarely needed those. For those, [mod://IPC::Run] seems like a good solution. And [mod://Capture::Tiny] is also an excellent module, it's useful if you also want to capture the output of the Perl process itself. Update: [mod://IPC::System::Simple], which the AM also mentioned, is also nice in that it provides drop-in replacements for [doc://system] and [doc://perlop#qx/_STRING_/|qx] with much better error handling (it's what [doc://autodie] uses when you say use autodie qw/system/;).

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
